statement: If Y = c + BX is an affine transformation of X ~ N(μ, Σ), where c is a constant M×1 vector and B is a constant M×N matrix, then Y is multivariate normally distributed: Y ~ N(c + Bμ, BΣB^T). The source states this result directly as a fact about affine transformations of multivariate normal vectors; it does not show the change-of-variables computation (density transformation or moment derivation) that produces the mean c+Bμ and covariance BΣB^T — only the final formula is given, so there is no derivation to restate from this source.

symbols.meaning: multivariate normal random vector being transformed

properties.property: Y = c + BX is itself multivariate normally distributed, i.e. an affine map of a Gaussian vector is Gaussian.
properties.why: stated directly as the conclusion of the affine transformation fact
given as the mean parameter of Y's distribution in the affine transformation statement
given as the covariance parameter of Y's distribution in the affine transformation statement

properties.property: Normality of a vector is equivalent to every linear combination of its components being univariate normal, which is consistent with (and underlies) why a linear/affine image of a normal vector is again normal.
properties.why: this is the defining property of multivariate normality given at the start of the source

assumptions.assumption: c is a constant M×1 vector and B is a constant M×N matrix (not functions of X or other random quantities).
assumptions.breaks_when: B or c depend on X or on other randomness, in which case the map is no longer affine and the stated result does not apply

assumptions.assumption: X ~ N(μ, Σ) is itself multivariate normal to begin with.
assumptions.breaks_when: X is not jointly Gaussian, in which case an affine transform need not be Gaussian

failure_modes.signature: Y's covariance matrix is not invertible, so Y has a degenerate (lower-dimensional) normal distribution
failure_modes.cause: B has rank less than M (fewer independent rows than the output dimension), or Σ itself is singular

shape: expected a derivation, produced a definition
